_why: PLAT-03, PLAT-04. The grid-sandbox PROFILE's checks file. It lives here beside the script triple rather than at labs/mN/checks.json — that second path is the MODULE checks path C1 and C6 read for truth_contract, and a profile is not a module, so this file carries no Truth Contract tag at all. EVERY ENTRY ASSERTS OBJECT STATE AND NONE ASSERTS A PERFORMANCE NUMBER (TRUST-06): a throughput or latency figure asserted by a learner's own checks file fails on a slower laptop and teaches the learner that the course is wrong. THE ENTRY THAT EARNS THIS FILE ITS KEEP IS probe-pod-reports-the-sandbox-kernel, and the reason is the reason the whole profile exists: a RuntimeClass is only a NAME, and a Pod on the DEFAULT RUNTIME (one with no runtimeClassName, or a RuntimeClass whose handler names runc) reaches Running in a healthy cluster. A create that exits 0, a Ready node and a Running Pod are byte-identical between the sandboxed and the default-runtime case, so NO ASSERTION MADE FROM OUTSIDE THE POD CAN TELL THEM APART. A handler containerd does not know is not silent: the sandbox is never created and the Pod waits in ContainerCreating (plan 05-21a). The kernel identity read from inside is the only evidence, and that entry reads it. A CAPABILITY DIFFERENTIAL IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED ANYWHERE HERE: 'this file is unreadable inside and readable outside, therefore it is isolated' is an overclaim SPIKE-01's own 'What the probe does not establish' section forbids — the differential shows a DIFFERENT KERNEL, which is an identity fact, and says nothing about kernel escapes, side channels or supply chain. matches is preferred over absent throughout, because the runner merges stderr into stdout and an absent assertion fails the moment any unrelated warning carries the forbidden substring. EVERY kubectl RUN SETS KUBECONFIG ITSELF, and that is a measured requirement rather than belt-and-braces: create.sh exports KUBECONFIG=/tmp/grid-sandbox.kubeconfig, but an export inside a script dies with the script, so the learner's own shell has no context and a bare `kubectl --context kind-grid-sandbox` fails with `context was not found`. THE NODE IMAGE IS ASSERTED BY TAG AND THAT IS THE ONE ENUMERATED DIGEST-PIN EXEMPTION: the image is built on the learner's own machine by labs/sandbox/runsc-node/build.sh, never pulled and never published, so there is no registry round-trip for a digest to protect — its own BASE is pinned by index digest inside that Dockerfile. PATH NOTE for plan 03-10: the one run that needs the shared helper resolves the repository root with git and then references labs/tools/...; the public labs tree strips the labs/ prefix for the Grid spine, so the sync path owns reconciling that.

checks.describe: the node count READ FROM THE CLUSTER equals 1 control-plane + lab.sizes.<SIZE>.worker_nodes — read, never taken from SIZE, because one cluster name serves both sizes
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && bash -c 'set -eu; export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-sandbox.kubeconfig}"; t=tools/size-gate.sh; [ -f "$t" ] || t=labs/$t; . "./$t"; assert_size; want=$((1 + $(size_value worker_nodes))); got=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-sandbox get nodes --no-headers | wc -l | tr -d " "); printf "node-count got=%s want=%s\n" "$got" "$want"'

checks.describe: every kubelet reports the pinned Kubernetes 1.37 minor — the node image is built FROM a digest-pinned 1.37.0 base, so a different minor means a different base
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-sandbox.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-sandbox get nodes -o json | jq -r '"kubelets=" + ([.items[].status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion | sub("\\.[0-9]+$"; "")] | unique | join(","))'

checks.describe: the API server writes the audit log M11 reads its denied-mutation evidence from (plan 05-04, CONTEXT D-30): both audit flags are read from the RUNNING kube-apiserver static Pod's command, never inferred from create.sh, because a kubeadm patch in a dialect kind does not match is dropped in silence and the cluster still comes up healthy. The policy file is baked into the node image, so --audit-policy-file names an in-image path; --audit-log-path names a FILE on the node, /var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log, which a restart of the node container keeps (review WR-03 measured the API server's stdout losing the evidence). Printed sorted, so the order is fixed and the anchored regex refuses either flag missing or the log sent anywhere else, stdout included
checks.run: bash -c 'set -eu; export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-sandbox.kubeconfig}"; A=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-sandbox -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-grid-sandbox-control-plane -o jsonpath="{.spec.containers[0].command[*]}"); for f in $A; do case "$f" in --audit-policy-file=*|--audit-log-path=*) printf "%s\n" "$f" ;; esac; done | LC_ALL=C sort | tr "\n" " "'

checks.describe: the RuntimeClass object exists and its handler matches the containerd stanza name the node image registered. The object alone proves NOTHING about the node — applying it to a stock cluster succeeds too — which is why the next two entries exist
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-sandbox.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-sandbox get runtimeclass runsc -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}/{.handler}'

checks.describe: the runtime handler is registered in EVERY node's own containerd configuration, read from inside each node container and printed as handler_nodes=k/n (review IN-04: at SIZE=16 the probe Pod tolerates everything and can run on either worker, so reading the control plane alone did not cover the node that ran it). Asserted BEFORE the Pod entry so a failure there can distinguish a missing handler from a Pod-level problem — they have different remedies
checks.run: n=0; k=0; for c in $(kind get nodes --name grid-sandbox 2>/dev/null); do n=$((n + 1)); if docker exec "$c" cat /etc/containerd/config.toml 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -q 'containerd.runtimes.runsc\]'; then k=$((k + 1)); fi; done; echo "handler_nodes=$k/$n"

checks.describe: THE ENTRY THAT EARNS THIS FILE ITS KEEP. A Pod under runtimeClassName: runsc reports the sandbox kernel identity read from INSIDE ITSELF. A Running phase proves nothing: a Pod on the default runtime (one with no runtimeClassName, or a RuntimeClass whose handler names runc) is Running in a healthy cluster too, indistinguishable from success anywhere outside the Pod. A handler missing from containerd is not silent: the Pod never starts. This is an IDENTITY assertion, never a security one
checks.run: bash -c 'set -eu; export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-sandbox.kubeconfig}"; K="kubectl --context kind-grid-sandbox"; $K delete pod checks-runsc-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=true --timeout=120s >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; if $K get pod checks-runsc-probe >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo stale-probe-still-present; exit 0; fi; printf "%s\n" "apiVersion: v1" "kind: Pod" "metadata: {name: checks-runsc-probe}" "spec:" "  runtimeClassName: runsc" "  restartPolicy: Never" "  tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]" "  containers:" "  - name: probe" "    image: busybox@sha256:bdf57e528e45e4433820e045b29b4597825a1c9e38353532d90a01445013f82e" "    command: [sh, -c, sleep 300]" | $K apply -f - >/dev/null; $K wait --for=condition=Ready pod/checks-runsc-probe --timeout=180s >/dev/null; V=$($K exec checks-runsc-probe -- cat /proc/version); $K delete pod checks-runsc-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; printf "in-pod /proc/version: %s\n" "$V"'

checks.describe: the node container was created from the LOCALLY BUILT node image, which is the create-time-immutable decision that makes grid-sandbox a profile rather than an addon layer. Asserted by tag: the one enumerated exemption from the digest-pin rule, because this image is never pulled and never published
